subject: Post-call: Mercato inference fit + recommended deployment path
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@mercato.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@mercatoinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Mercato inference fit + recommended deployment path

Alex / Maya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency on current self-hosted setup (spikes to >400ms p95 for short prompts used in search/query use cases). This is directly affecting product conversion.
- Goal: 100–150ms p95 for text-generation-style prompts (avg token window ~32 tokens) and sustained 200–300 req/s during business hours.
- Constraints: sensitive PII in prompts, must meet MFA/SSO + audit logs; procurement timeline ~Q3.

Technical notes (from today’s deep-dive)
- Typical request profile: 6–40 tokens output, 32 token context, ~70% short-request distribution.
- Preferred model family: ~13B dense or 13B-quantized (they noted internal benchmarks on Llama3-13B).
- KV cache behavior: warm-cache expected for ~60% of requests (search reranks), prefix caching beneficial.

Recommended deployment options (tradeoffs)
1) Redwood Dedicated (recommended starting point)
   - Config: 2x A100 or 4x A10 equivalent instances with model quantized to 4-bit.
   - Rationale: predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency targets, private networking option for PII.
   - Expected baseline: ~130ms p95 at 200 req/s with prefix caching and batching set to conservative 12ms window.
2) Hosted API + VPC egress (short term test)
   - Use hosted for canary traffic (~10% of requests) to validate end-to-end latency and correctness before committing to Dedicated.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Diego: share annotated topology diagram and latency-test plan (attached) — today (sent).
- Mercato: provide representative curl + sample prompt set (10–20 queries) to run local latency baseline — by EOD 2028-07-13.
- Karthik/Marissa: produce a pricing sketch for Dedicated/hosted hybrid and a proposed rollout plan (canary -> 50% -> full) — by 2028-07-15.

Attachments: mercato-postcall-notes.pdf (topology + perf assumptions), latency-test-plan.csv (sample prompts + expected metrics).

If anything above is off, call it out — otherwise we’ll proceed with the test plan on your sample prompts.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@mercato.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@mercatoinc.com>
Date: 2028-07-11T17:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Mercato inference fit + recommended deployment path

Diego — thanks for the crisp recap. A couple clarifications and notes from our side: 

Clarifications
- The 400ms spikes are for single-token generation in our reranker pipeline when multiple microservices are chained; most user-visible latency is p95 of the full pipeline.
- Data residency: Compute must live in our AWS account inside a private subnet (we can do VPC peering or shared VPC).

What we’ll provide
- A 20-query sample set and a short script to reproduce our current baseline this week (I’ll upload to the Drive link you shared).
- SOC2 evidence and contract point-of-contact for procurement (expect to share early next week).

One ask
- Can your latency-test plan include a cold-start scenario and an explicit KV-cache warm path so we can see both numbers? We need to understand worst-case and typical-case.

I’m copying Maya for procurement alignment. Thanks — we’re aligned to run the tests.

— Alex
Alex Novak | Head of ML Platforms, Mercato

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@mercato.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@mercatoinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Mercato inference fit + recommended deployment path

Perfect — thanks Alex. I’ve updated the test plan to include:
- Cold-start (empty KV cache, cold model load)
- Warm path (KV cache primed with top 10k prefixes)
- 95th/99th latency buckets, CPU/GPU utilization, and token throughput.

Quick note on sizing: if your sample set shows >300ms p95 on the warm path, we’ll recommend increasing concurrent instances (scale-out) or switching to higher-memory GPUs to reduce batching latency. We’ll run the initial tests on Redwood-hosted infra inside your VPC (private egress) to avoid any data transfers.

I’ve attached the CSV with the sample prompts format and a short checklist for the test run. When you drop the script, we’ll run against our staging harness and share a result sheet.

— Diego

(attachment: latency-test-plan.csv)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T16:45:00Z
Subject: Internal: Mercato follow-up — immediate asks

Marissa / Karthik — short internal checklist before we start the run: 
- Karthik: prep a concise recommendation page for 2x config options (2x A100 / 4x A10 equiv) with expected p95 and cost per 1M tokens. Include fallback routing plan (hosted->dedicated) and automatic model variant failover.
- Marissa: open HS record and start procurement intro (attach SOC2 + standard SOW template).
- My ask: keep the canary size small (10% traffic) and ensure we can trace tokens through the pipeline to isolate non-inference bottlenecks.

I’ll be on call with their infra team tomorrow at 11:00 PT to walk the VPC peering checklist.

— Diego

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@mercato.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@mercatoinc.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-13T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Mercato inference fit + recommended deployment path

Alex / Maya — welcome aboard. I’ve created HS-123456 (procurement thread) and attached our SOC 2 pack and SOW template to the Drive link. Diego — I’ll send the pricing sketch by EOD Monday with two committed options and a short ops SLA addendum for audit logging.

Next immediate milestone: run results posted (Redwood) once Alex uploads the sample script. We’ll aim for a readout the same week and propose a canary window.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
